name: SlimLipo

lead: SlimLipo is a brand of laser lipolysis. A thin laser fiber is placed under the skin to liquefy fat.
People use it for contouring small areas and for some skin tightening.

paras: Laser energy liquefies fat and coagulates tissue, which tightens the overlying skin.
As with liposuction generally: bleeding, infection, clots, contour irregularities. Fat can redistribute over months.

chain: Laser fiber liquefies fat under the skin
Slimmer contour with some skin tightening
angle.text: People use it to reduce stubborn local fat deposits and sharpen contours such as the jawline, waist or flanks.

lead: SlimLipo is a brand of laser lipolysis, a cosmetic procedure that uses laser energy to liquefy small pockets of fat for removal, aimed at body and neck contouring. Laser-assisted liposuction is also called laser lipolysis or "Smart Lipo," and uses laser energy to liquefy fat and to coagulate and tighten skin.[1]
It is used for contouring areas such as ankles, and general liposuction is the most common cosmetic procedure in the US as of 2015.[1]

paras: Laser-assisted liposuction liquefies fat and coagulates tissue to tighten skin.[1] Liposuction in general is for contouring rather than weight loss, and fat tends to return and redistribute after a few months.[1]
Modern liposuction began with European surgeons in the late 1960s; the Fischers developed a blunt-cannula technique in the mid-1970s and Klein introduced tumescent anesthesia in the 1980s.[1]

General liposuction risks include deep vein thrombosis, organ perforation, bleeding, infection, seromas, skin necrosis and lidocaine toxicity, with roughly one death per 10,000 cases cited as of 2011.[1] Laser-specific risks are not detailed in this source.

timeline.event: Liposuction becomes the most common US cosmetic procedure.[1]
